summary: Tested CityQuest MVP — backend 19/19 pytest tests PASS (100%). Frontend mobile UI flows largely working: Explore screen + category chip filter, city picker (Gaziantep→Rome switch reflects in header), Quest difficulty filter + tap into detail, Skip-GPS fallback, trivia incorrect path (shows 'Try Again'), trivia correct path (Quest Complete + XP + badge), Profile name edit persists, Food search filter works (2 cards → 1 on 'baklava'), Leaderboard renders sorted. CRITICAL issue: Map tab shows 'React Native WebView does not support this platform.' in web preview — react-native-webview has no web fallback. Minor: React Native Web deprecation warnings ('shadow*' style props, props.pointerEvents).

ui_bugs.issue: react-native-webview is not supported on web. Map shows the literal text 'React Native WebView does not support this platform.' Need a Platform.OS === 'web' branch that renders the same Leaflet HTML inside an <iframe srcDoc={html}> so the web preview works. Native (Expo Go/native build) is fine. Reference: /app/frontend/app/(tabs)/map.tsx:83

issues: When the result card is shown (success or fail), the bottom action bar still contains the 'Skip GPS — Continue' button alongside 'Done'/'Try again'. This is confusing post-result; Skip GPS should be hidden once result is shown. Reference: /app/frontend/app/quest/[id].tsx around the bottom action bar.

react_native_issues.issue: Deprecation warnings in console: '"shadow*" style props are deprecated. Use "boxShadow".' and 'props.pointerEvents is deprecated. Use style.pointerEvents.' Likely in components using shadowColor/shadowOpacity/shadowRadius (e.g., card styles). Reference: search /app/frontend for shadowColor / shadowOpacity / pointerEvents.

action_items: Add Platform.OS === 'web' branch in app/(tabs)/map.tsx that renders <iframe srcDoc={html} style={{flex:1,border:0}} /> instead of <WebView />. This is the only blocking issue.
Hide the 'Skip GPS — Continue' button once the result card is shown in quest/[id].tsx (conditional on !result).
Migrate shadowColor/shadowOpacity/shadowRadius/shadowOffset to boxShadow (or use elevation cross-platform) and move pointerEvents from prop to style to silence deprecation warnings.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is well-structured and uses {'_id': 0} projections — no ObjectId leakage.
Check-in idempotency, level-up flag, badge unlock, and persistence all behave correctly under tests.
Map screen relies on react-native-webview which has no web implementation; should be platform-branched.
_layout in (tabs) uses tabBarButtonTestID (good) — works in Expo Router v3+.
No deprecated expo-av / expo-barcode-scanner / expo-background-fetch usage found.
seed_data_creation: No manual seeding. Backend auto-seeds 4 cities / 19 POIs / 14 quests on startup. Test runs created 3 progress docs (TEST_* device_ids) which are visible in the leaderboard with display_name 'Traveler'. Safe to ignore or clean up later.

Pytest suite at /app/backend/tests/test_cityquest.py is the regression set (19 tests, ~1.7s). For UI: use viewport 390x844 and testIDs listed in the screens (tab-explore, tab-map, tab-quest, tab-food, tab-profile, explore-screen, explore-chip-{cat}, city-picker-button, city-option-{id}, quest-screen, quest-chip-{diff}, quest-card-{id}, quest-detail, quest-start-btn, quest-skip-gps, trivia-card, trivia-option-{i}, quest-submit-trivia, result-card, food-screen, food-card-{id}, map-screen, profile-screen, profile-name-edit/input/save). The map web fallback (iframe srcDoc) is the only known blocker. Trivia correct indices verified: q-gaz-1=0, q-gaz-2=2, q-gaz-3=1, q-rom-1=2.
rca_of_issue: MapScreen RCA: react-native-webview package only ships native (iOS/Android) implementations. On react-native-web, it falls back to a stub that renders the text 'React Native WebView does not support this platform.' Fix is to detect Platform.OS === 'web' and render an <iframe srcDoc={html} /> with the same Leaflet HTML (or use react-native-web-webview shim). Reproduction: open the deployed web preview, tap the Map tab — the leaflet map never loads and the platform-not-supported message is visible.
